text:
Colton Dach is an Edmonton kid playing for his hometown team, and he's been a useful one. The 23-year-old, a 2021 second-rounder by Chicago, has five points in 15 games for the Oilers. He missed a couple of games with an illness this month (CBS Sports) and came back with an assist against Philadelphia on Nov. 11.

His finishing is honest. He's shooting 10.3%, with three goals on 2.9 expected, and his chance rate is up from last season. The concern is the other end: Edmonton gets just 41% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, more than nine points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey's note from last season helps explain some of it, since he played with weak linemates and his team created little offense with him on.

He's a 6-foot-3 physical winger with 36 hits, and the Oilers use him in 14-minute doses. Of the 107 forwards picked 52nd to 72nd since 2005 with four-plus seasons, 42 reached 200 NHL games. He's on his way. What we'd watch is whether he can be on the ice for more chances for than against.
